info.description:
The CoderHelm API lets your own programs start and follow CoderHelm's work: list and inspect runs, retry or cancel them, create and run plans, read the reviewer's reviews, and check token usage.

Every request is authenticated with a team API key sent as a bearer token. Admins create keys in the dashboard under Settings, API keys. A key holds scopes, never more than the admin who made it, and has its own rate limit.

CI jobs upload test reports with a GitHub Actions OIDC token instead of a key, and the webhooks are verified by their signatures.

post.description: Subscribe CoderHelm to an SNS topic with an HTTPS subscription to this address and add the topic under Alert routes in the dashboard. Every message's SNS signature is checked (signature versions 1 and 2) and the signing certificate must come from SNS. post.description: Takes one test report from a CI job whose results never reach GitHub (a device farm, say), signed with the job's GitHub Actions OIDC token instead of a CoderHelm secret. Request the token with the audience `coderhelm`. CoderHelm checks it was issued for a workflow run of a repository connected to your team with E2E results turned on, then reads the report like one from GitHub: flaky tests, failure groups and quarantine.

requestBody.description: The report file, at most 6 MB.

post.description: Where GitHub sends every event of the CoderHelm GitHub App. Installing the app sets this up; you only call it yourself when you self-host. Each request is signed with the app's webhook secret in `X-Hub-Signature-256` (`sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body), compared in constant time. The event type comes from `X-GitHub-Event` and the body must name an installation. Events CoderHelm doesn't act on, and events from an installation not linked to a team, are accepted with `200` and ignored.

parameters.description: The event type, such as `issues`, `pull_request` or `push`.
parameters.name: X-GitHub-Event

requestBody.description: The event payload, as GitHub defines it for each event type. It must include `installation.id`.

400.description: The body is not JSON or names no installation.

401.description: The signature is missing or wrong.

post.description: For a plain Jira webhook, when the CoderHelm Jira app can't be installed. The URL holds a token generated for your team on the Jira page of the dashboard. If you also generated a secret there, every request must carry `X-Hub-Signature`: `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with that secret. Jira Cloud signs webhooks this way when you set the secret on the webhook; a Jira automation can send the header itself.

parameters.description: The webhook token from the Jira page of the dashboard.
parameters.name: token

200.description: Accepted (whether or not it started anything).

401.description: Unknown token, or the signature is missing or wrong.

post.description: Tells CoderHelm that pages of a connected knowledge source changed, so it syncs that source now instead of at its next scheduled sync. Sanity posts to the address shown for each Sanity source (CoderHelm registers it itself when the token may manage webhooks), signed with `sanity-webhook-signature`: `t=<ms>,v1=` and the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<body>`, keyed with the token in the address; a signature older than five minutes is refused. Notion posts to `/webhooks/knowledge/notion` for the whole install, signed with `X-Notion-Signature`: `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body, keyed with the subscription's verification token. An event only starts a sync: what changed is always read back from the provider with the source's own connection.

parameters.description: The source's webhook token, or `notion` for the install's Notion subscription.
parameters.name: token

200.description: Accepted; a sync starts unless the source is paused.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong or too old.
